decision_summary: Sheriff John Allen announced the decision to end BCSO's Flock Safety contracts in a Sept. 3 official statement, citing lost confidence in Flock's privacy safeguards and data sharing. Three contracts ended: five ALPR cameras, 16 speed cameras connected to the Flock network, and gunshot detection technology. BCSO is replacing Flock with Axon ALPR technology.

decision_summary: 60-month Flock agreement signed 2024-09-12 with 24-month renewal term; $141,850 annual recurring platform cost; 15 Falcon ALPRs plus 6 solar multi-purpose LPR/video units; 30-day retention. City council added privacy rules in September 2026 requiring a public Flock data portal and affidavits from out-of-state agencies.

decision_summary: Active Flock network of 19 cameras reported August 2026. Program began with vehicle-mounted cameras in 2018, moved to fixed units in 2020. On Sept. 10, 2026 residents pressed the city council to end Flock; no cancellation or formal action was reported. Data deleted after 30 days unless retained for a case.
